Coefficient, distribution and influence plot for one term

Source: R/influence.R
plot_cdi_comps.Rd

A coefficient-distribution-influence plot (Bentley et al. 2011) for one term of influ_comps(), with the axes shared between the panels.

  • Centre: the distribution of the data. Bubbles show the share of the data in each level of the term (x) in each year (y).

  • Top, sharing the level axis (x): the effect of each level on every bin (y), as the log of the multiplier relative to the geometric mean over levels. Bars extend to the right (more fish in the bin than average) or to the left (fewer), with 95% intervals. Bar lengths are scaled to the largest effect, and a scale bar gives the reference length. With many levels, a heat map replaces the bars. Cells whose interval includes zero are faded.

  • Right, sharing the year axis (y): the influence of the term on the annual composition in every bin (x), as the log ratio of the predicted proportion with and without the term. Cells whose interval includes zero are faded.

Orange is below and skyblue above the reference.

Usage

plot_cdi_comps(
  influ,
  term,
  component = NULL,
  var = NULL,
  style = c("auto", "bars", "tile"),
  max_levels = 10,
  xlab = "Length bin (cm)"
)

Arguments

influ

Output of influ_comps().

term

Term (a name in influ$groups, i.e. a variable, or the joint random-effect label).

component

"catch" or "index", for the distribution and influence panels.

var

Variable whose levels are shown, for a term that groups several variables. Default: the first.

style

"auto" (bars for up to max_levels levels, otherwise a heat map), "bars" or "tile".

max_levels

Maximum number of levels shown as bars with style = "auto".

xlab

Label of the bin axis.

Value

A patchwork of ggplots.

References

Bentley, N., Kendrick, T.H., Starr, P.J., Breen, P.A. (2012). Influence plots and metrics: tools for better understanding fisheries catch-per-unit-effort standardizations. ICES Journal of Marine Science 69, 84-88.
